app.name: Node64
app.tagline: Health checks, DynDNS and more in your own network

setup.title: Welcome to Node64
setup.intro: Choose your language and create the local administrator. There is no default password.
setup.password_hint: At least 10 characters. Use a passphrase or a password manager.
setup.agent_name_hint: For example “Pi in the basement”. Shown later in the ipv64 portal, too.
setup.location_hint: For example Home, Office, Parents. A location can have several nodes.
setup.done: The node is set up. You can sign in now.

login.title: Sign in
login.ratelimited: Too many attempts. Please try again in {seconds} seconds.
login.totp_hint: Enter the code from your authenticator app or a recovery code.
login.totp_failed: The code is wrong or expired.

dashboard.edit_hint: Move tiles with the mouse (or the arrows), change the width with s/m/l/xl, show or hide with the eye. Hidden tiles appear faded here. “Done” saves for your user.
dashboard.api_none: No ipv64 API key stored. With a key the node shows all limits of your account here and talks to ipv64 directly (DynDNS, one-click linking).
dashboard.hc_hint: Optional, only for healthchecks: sync via the hub servers (online checks, live states, notifications via ipv64).
dashboard.mismatch: The API key belongs to a different account than the healthchecks sync.
dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.no_modules: No module is active yet. Enable Healthchecks in the settings.
dashboard.not_linked: Not linked. The node runs standalone.

cdn64.title: CDN64 · Reverse proxy
cdn64.empty: No proxy hosts yet. A proxy host forwards requests for a domain to a service in your home network.
cdn64.list_hint: Reachability: checked every minute. Requests: since the module started.
cdn64.edge_error: The common entrance cannot open a port:

f.names_hint: One per line (or comma separated), wildcards like *.example.ipv64.de too. The DNS record must point to this connection.
f.target_hint: The service in your home network, e.g. http://192.168.1.20:8123. The target gets the name the visitor used plus X-Forwarded-For/-Proto/-Host and X-Real-IP.
f.verify_target_hint: Off: self-signed certificates (Proxmox, UniFi, NAS) work too – like NPM.
f.cache_assets_hint: Keep images, CSS, JS and fonts in memory.
f.block_exploits_hint: Reject typical attacks (SQL and file injection, .git/.env) with 403.
f.websockets_hint: For services with live connections (e.g. Home Assistant).
f.cert_hint: Certificates come from the certificate manager (Let's Encrypt via ipv64 or your own). Without a matching certificate the browser shows a warning.
f.force_ssl_hint: Requests via http:// are redirected to https://.
f.hsts_hint: Browsers use only HTTPS for this domain for two years.
f.http3_hint: Needs 443/UDP on the router and the switch in the common entrance.
f.min_tls_hint: TLS 1.3 is current; 1.2 for older devices.
f.cert_new: Request a new certificate right away
f.cert_new_hint: For all domains of this host; the request runs in the background after saving.
f.redirect_hint: Domain, optionally with port and path (e.g. www.example.com/new). "Same as request" uses http or https as the visitor came.
f.dead_hint: This host answers every request with a neutral "404" page. With a certificate also via HTTPS.
f.pass_hint: The connection is handed raw to this target by name, without decrypting it here – the target needs its own certificate. Port 80 redirects to HTTPS.
f.access_hint: Access only with password and/or from certain networks.
f.locations_hint: Paths with their own target, e.g. /api to another service. The longest matching path wins; everything else goes to the host's target.
f.locations_more: Empty rows are ignored. For more locations save and edit again.
f.adv_headers_hint: One "Name: value" or name per line. Connection headers (Connection, Upgrade, Content-Length …) cannot be changed.
f.adv_limits_hint: Timeout: how long to wait for the target's answer, 0 = no limit. Upload: larger requests get 413, 0 = unlimited.
f.adv_trusted_hint: If a request comes from these networks, the IP from CF-Connecting-IP or X-Forwarded-For counts as the real client IP (for target, access lists and log). Otherwise the connection's peer always counts.
f.adv_access_log_hint: Every request individually under "Requests". The hourly counters always run.

err.name: Invalid domain name.
err.scheme: Scheme must be http or https.
err.redirect_self: A redirection to itself would loop.
err.stream_port_edge: Port {name} belongs to the common entrance (HTTP/HTTPS). For services on 443 by name: "TLS passthrough".
err.location_target: Target of location {name} is missing or invalid.
err.acl_password: Password missing or longer than 72 characters: {name}
err.acl_empty: At least one user or IP rule.
err.no_target: This host has no target to check.
err.dns_content: Invalid target (domain for CNAME, IPv4 for A, IPv6 for AAAA).

cdn64.help_ports: The router forwards 80 and 443 (TCP, for HTTP/3 also 443/UDP) to this node. Node64 distributes the rest by domain name – also together with DNS64 in the same container.
cdn64.help_certs: For domains at ipv64 there are Let's Encrypt certificates via the API key, without port 80 being open.
cdn64.help_dns: The domain must point to your connection via DNS, e.g. as a CNAME to your DynDNS domain.

kind_empty.proxy: No proxy hosts yet. A proxy host forwards requests for a domain to a service in your home network.
kind_empty.redirect: No redirections yet. A redirection sends visitors of one domain to another (e.g. old domain to new).
kind_empty.dead: No 404 hosts yet. A 404 host deliberately answers a domain with "not found", e.g. for retired names.

streams.title: Streams (TCP/UDP)
streams.empty: No streams yet. A stream forwards a port raw to a service, e.g. for game servers, MQTT or WireGuard.
streams.hint: Streams occupy their port per protocol; Settings → Ports shows overlaps. UDP sessions end after 60 s without packets.

f.name: Name (optional)
f.hint: Target in the home network. A port can only be opened once per protocol.
f.tls_hint: With a certificate the stream accepts TLS and forwards unencrypted to the target.

streams.help_ports: Forward the port (TCP and/or UDP) on the router to this node. Ports below 1024 work without root thanks to the image's capabilities.
streams.help_docker: With host networking Node64 opens the port directly. In bridge mode the port must also be published on the container (-p).

pass.title: TLS passthrough (port 443 by name)
pass.hint: For services that should do TLS themselves (own certificate, e.g. a second proxy): the connection is passed on raw by name, everything else on 443 stays with Node64.

default.title: Default page for unknown names
default.hint: What Node64 answers on port 80/443 when a name belongs to no host or someone calls the IP directly.
default.mode_hint_close: no answer, like nginx 444; reveals the least
default.html_hint: Served with status 200; without external scripts it loads fastest.

cdn64.create_check: Create a healthcheck for this target

acl.name: Name
acl.all_long: Both required: allowed IP and login (where set up)
acl.any_long: One condition is enough: allowed IP or login
acl.pass_auth: Pass the login on to the target
acl.pass_auth_hint: Off: the target does not see the Authorization header.
acl.users_hint: New or changed users as "name:password", one per line. Passwords are stored hashed only (bcrypt).
acl.rules_hint: One "allow" or "deny" and an IP, a network or "all" per line. The first match counts, without a match access is denied.
acl.empty: No access lists yet. They restrict hosts by password and/or to certain networks.
acl.hint: After 10 failed logins within 5 minutes the IP is blocked for 15 minutes (recorded in the audit log).
acl.help: Typical: only from the home network ("allow 192.168.0.0/16") and with password when away – then "one condition is enough".

log.no_db: Statistics are not available (module just started or file not writable).
log.none_enabled: No host has the access log switched on (edit host → Advanced).
log.settings_hint: Hourly counters are kept for 90 days. Stored in cdn64.db, not in the node backup.

dnsrec.hint: For every domain of this host that is in your ipv64 account. Recommended: CNAME to your DynDNS domain kept current by the updater. Existing records stay unchanged; no CNAME for the domain itself.

certs.title: Certificates
certs.empty: No certificates yet. For domains at ipv64, Node64 gets them from Let's Encrypt via the API key.
certs.delete_used: Certificate "{name}" is used by: {hosts}. Delete anyway? These hosts will no longer have a valid certificate.
certs.cname_needed: Required CNAME records at the domain's provider
certs.hint: Renewal is automatic 30 days before expiry; on errors and 14 or 3 days before expiry the default channels get a message. Keys are stored encrypted in the database.
certs.email_hint: Let's Encrypt only writes about problems with certificates.
certs.tos_accept: I accept the Let's Encrypt terms of service
certs.dns_missing: No ipv64 API key: DNS-01 via ipv64 needs a key.
certs.http_ready: HTTP-01 via port 80 of the common entrance
certs.names_hint: One per line, wildcards too (*.example.ipv64.de, DNS only). At most 100 names.

src_hint.auto: ipv64 DNS-01 if all names are in the ipv64 account, otherwise HTTP-01.
src_hint.ipv64: for domains in the ipv64 account; wildcards too, port 80 need not be open.
src_hint.alias: for domains at other providers: set a CNAME once, ipv64 does the rest – no provider credentials needed.
src_hint.http: port 80 must reach this node from outside; no wildcards.
src_hint.dns: for domains at Cloudflare, Hetzner, netcup, INWX, IONOS and others: Node64 sets the TXT record via their API (store an account).
src_hint.ca: for devices in your own network, also for IP addresses and names like nas.lan; devices have to trust the CA once.

certs.alias_hint: Create this CNAME for each name at your provider. Node64 checks it before the request.
certs.staging_hint: For trying things out without rate limits; no browser trusts such certificates.
certs.upload_hint: Certificate with chain and the matching private key, as PEM (file or pasted).
certs.upload_safe: The key is stored encrypted and never shown again.
certs.host_saved_cert: Saved. Certificate for {name} is being requested.
certs.host_saved_no_cert: Host saved, but no certificate requested: {error}

err.tos: Please accept the Let's Encrypt terms of service first.
err.nokey: This method needs the ipv64 API key (settings).
err.in_use: The certificate is still in use.
err.busy: This certificate is being requested right now.
err.name: Check the name
err.no_cert: The certificate has not been issued yet.
err.key_password: The key is protected by a password. Please enter the password.

dns.title: DNS accounts
dns.name: Name
dns.hint: Credentials are stored encrypted and only used for Let's Encrypt TXT records. Ideally create a key with DNS rights only.
dns.empty: For domains at other providers: store an account, then DNS-01 works there too (wildcards included).
dns.account_hint: The provider must manage the domain.

dl.title: Download
dl.pem: Everything in one file (.pem, e.g. HAProxy, Fritzbox)
dl.p12_password_hint: 4 to 128 characters. It is asked for on import and not stored.
dl.p12_legacy: Old encryption (3DES) for older devices and Windows versions
dl.api_hint: For scripts on other devices: GET /api/certs/{id}/bundle?format=zip|fullchain|key|pem with an API key; ETag and If-None-Match only reload on change. Every download with key is in the audit log.

ca.title: Own CAs
ca.empty: For devices in your own network (nas.lan, 192.168.x.x): create or import a CA, then issue certificates with it.
ca.delete_confirm: Delete CA “{name}”? Devices that trust it keep it until it is removed there.
ca.names_hint: Names and IP addresses (one per line). Up to 825 days (Apple's limit); renewed in the last third, at most 30 days before expiry.
ca.create_hint: Node64 creates key and CA certificate (10 years). The key stays encrypted in the database and is part of the backup.
ca.name: Name
ca.constrain_hint: The CA may then only confirm names like *.lan, *.home.arpa, *.internal, *.local and private IPs. Even if its key is stolen, no internet domains can be forged with it.
ca.domains: Additionally allowed domains (optional, one per line)
ca.import_hint: The CA certificate (with chain for an intermediate CA) and its private key as PEM, e.g. from step-ca, OpenSSL or XCA.
ca.in_use: CA “{name}” still has issued certificates. Delete them or move them to another CA first.

acme.title: ACME CAs
acme.hint: Besides Let's Encrypt you can use other CAs that speak ACME: ZeroSSL, Google Trust Services, SSL.com or your own step-ca.
acme.eab_hint: External Account Binding: required by ZeroSSL, Google and SSL.com, created in the CA's account. The HMAC is stored encrypted.
acme.root_hint: Only for your own CA such as step-ca whose certificate is not publicly trusted.
acme.tos: I accept the terms of service of this CA.
acme.in_use: Certificates still use the ACME CA “{name}”. Delete or move them first.

why.nohttp: the shared entrance (port 80) is not available

certs.upload_password: Password of the key or the .pfx/.p12 file (only if encrypted)
certs.upload_password_hint: Purchased certificates often come with an encrypted key (ENCRYPTED PRIVATE KEY, DEK-Info) or as .pfx/.p12. Instead of certificate and key you can also put a .pfx/.p12 file into the certificate field. Only the decrypted key is stored (encrypted in the database), the password is not.

ports.title: Ports
ports.hint: Which ports Node64 uses or wants to use. A port can only be opened once per address; modules share 80 and 443 through the common entrance.
ports.edge_hint: Opens the ports only while a module needs them (e.g. CDN64 or Let's Encrypt via HTTP-01). Forward 80 and 443 (TCP, for HTTP/3 also 443/UDP) on the router to this node.
ports.edge_public_hint: Only needed if the router forwards a different port (e.g. 443 → 8443). Empty = same as HTTPS port.
ports.err_port: Ports must be between 0 and 65535 (0 = off).
ports.ui_public: Also reachable from the internet (not recommended)
ports.ui_hint: The Node64 interface is then also reachable at https://<name>, with a certificate from the manager. Default: only from your own network (private networks, Tailscale); everyone else gets a neutral 404.
ports.ui_cert: Certificate of the web interface (HTTPS port and name at the entrance)
ports.ui_cert_auto: Automatic: matching certificate for the requested name, otherwise self-signed
ports.ui_cert_env: NODE64_TLS_CERT is set: the HTTPS port uses this file, the choice only applies to the name at the entrance.
ports.ui_cert_hint: Changes apply without restart. Certificates come from the central manager:

settings.appearance_hint: Applies immediately, for this browser. Everything scales along, on phones and tablets too.
settings.title: Settings
settings.modules_hint: A disabled module does not run, uses no resources and has no menu entry. Its configuration is kept.
settings.password_changed: Password changed. Other sessions were signed out.
settings.data_hint: Applies to this node only. ipv64.net keeps its own data shorter (single measurements 2 days, hourly values 90 days). Longer retention needs more storage: about 13 MB per check and month of single measurements at a 60-second interval (365 days: about 160 MB per check).
settings.data_chart_standard: Standard – every measurement up to 24 hours, hourly averages for 7 and 30 days, daily averages for 1 year
settings.data_chart_fine: Fine – every measurement up to 7 days, hourly averages for 30 days and 1 year
settings.data_chart_finest: Finest – every measurement up to 30 days, hourly averages for 1 year
settings.data_chart_hint: Finer levels show more points and load slower. Before the kept single measurements, hourly or daily values are used.
settings.log_level_hint: Debug shows request details, DNS resolution and timings. Secrets stay masked.
settings.updates_hint: Only fetches a version file from ipv64.net, no data is sent.

errors.title: Error
errors.csrf: The form has expired. Please reload the page and submit again.
errors.internal: Internal error. Details are in the log.
errors.password_short: The password needs at least 10 characters.
errors.username_invalid: The username may only contain letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore (3 to 64 characters).

ipv64key.title: ipv64 API key
ipv64key.hint: One API key for all modules of this container: the DynDNS updater, for example, uses it to fetch domains, records, tokens and the update limit. Enter it once here.
ipv64key.placeholder_new: new API key (empty = check the stored one)
ipv64key.stored_hint: Checked at ipv64 and stored encrypted on this node. An API key has full rights in the account, so only enter it on your own devices.
ipv64key.create_link: Create an API key at ipv64
ipv64key.remove_confirm: Remove the API key from this node? Modules that need it (e.g. picking in the DynDNS updater) will stop working. Configured DynDNS targets keep updating.
ipv64key.invalid: This does not look like an ipv64 API key (16 to 64 letters and digits).
ipv64key.rejected: ipv64 rejected the API key (wrong, expired or deleted).
ipv64key.expiry_warn: The API key expires soon. Create a new one at ipv64 in time and enter it here, otherwise the modules that need it stop working.

dyn.title: DynDNS updater
dyn.hint: Keeps selected domains and records at ipv64 up to date with the public address of this connection. Updates are only sent when the address has actually changed.

conn.title: Connection
conn.no_route6_hint: This container has no IPv6 connectivity. For IPv6 start the container with network_mode: host or enable IPv6 in the Docker network. IPv4 still works.
conn.temporary_hint: The IPv6 address seen from outside is a temporary privacy address and changes regularly. For AAAA records use "prefix + interface ID" or "interface" later.
conn.local6: Global IPv6 addresses of this host
conn.check_busy: The check takes longer, the result will show up in the log shortly.
conn.idle: No target is enabled, so the regular check is paused (no lookups, no entries); "Check now" still works.

targets.title: Targets
targets.name: Name
targets.enabled: Keep this target up to date
targets.exists: This name is already set up as a target.
targets.no_record: ipv64 has no A or AAAA record for this name anymore.

settings.title: Checking
settings.interval_hint: Looking up the own address does not count against the DynDNS update limit. Updates are only sent on a change.
settings.source_hint: Empty = ipv64. An own URL must return the address as text or JSON; ipv64 stays the fallback.
settings.invalid: Invalid input: check interval or URL (http/https only).
settings.notify_limit: Update limit almost or fully reached (at most once a day)
settings.notify_hint: Sent to the default channels of this node, even when it is linked with ipv64. ipv64 mail and SMS go directly through the API with the ipv64 API key, not via the hub servers. Nothing is sent during quiet hours; the history still shows everything.

net.cgnat: Possibly CGNAT: on the way to the internet there is hop {hop} from the provider NAT range 100.64.0.0/10. Then you share the IPv4 address with other customers and cannot be reached through it from outside, even if DynDNS sets it correctly. This cannot be detected with certainty from inside, but is very likely here.
net.dslite: Possibly DS-Lite: on the way to the internet there is the DS-Lite tunnel endpoint {hop}. IPv4 then runs over a shared provider address and cannot be reached from outside; you are reachable via IPv6. This cannot be detected with certainty from inside, but is very likely here.
net.ok: Path to the internet checked: no sign of CGNAT or DS-Lite.

api.title: ipv64 access
api.central: The API key is managed centrally in the settings.
api.hint: To pick domains from your account, enter the ipv64 API key once in the settings. Without a key, targets can be added manually.
api.needed: This needs the ipv64 API key in the settings.

dyn.mode4_hint: Automatic reports the public IPv4 of the connection (the router's). Behind CGNAT/DS-Lite the IPv4 cannot be reached from outside, then set IPv4 to "off".

mode6_hint.host: Reports the IPv6 address of this node as seen from outside. Fits with network_mode: host; temporary privacy addresses change regularly.
mode6_hint.prefix: Reports only the /64 prefix. ipv64 applies it to all AAAA records of the zone that only carry an interface ID (::1:2:3:4). Affects the whole zone.
mode6_hint.suffix: Combines the current /64 prefix with the interface ID entered here and reports the full address for this record only. Good for LAN devices with a fixed interface ID.
mode6_hint.iface: Uses the stable global address of a network interface (temporary addresses are skipped). Only with network_mode: host.
mode6_hint.off: IPv6 is not updated for this name.

token_hint.record: Safest level: the token can only change this one name.
token_hint.domain: The domain token can change the whole domain including subhosts. Use a record token if possible.

pick.title: Domains and records of your account
pick.need_key: Picking from the account needs an API key:
pick.empty: The account has no active domains with A or AAAA records.
pick.hint: The record token is used (safest level). IPv4 and IPv6 are preset from the existing records and can be changed per target afterwards.
pick.modes_hint: Choose per name what gets updated; fixed addresses and the interface mode are available afterwards when editing. With "prefix + interface ID" the interface ID is taken from the existing AAAA record.

manual.title: Enter manually
manual.hint: Without an API key: enter domain, host and token yourself. The record token is shown at the record at ipv64, the domain token at the domain.

field.mode_none: enable at least IPv4 or IPv6

edit.no_ifaces: No global IPv6 addresses visible. This mode needs network_mode: host.
edit.modes_help: What do the IPv6 modes mean?
edit.delete_confirm: Stop updating {name}? The record stays at ipv64.

pause_hint.badauth: ipv64 rejected the token, e.g. because it was regenerated. Use "Fetch token again" or enter a new token, then "Update now".
pause_hint.nohost: This name does not exist (anymore) at ipv64. Check it at ipv64 or delete the target.
pause_hint.conflict: A CNAME, CDN or failover on the name prevents the update. Resolve it at ipv64, then "Update now".
pause_hint.flapping: The record was set differently from elsewhere several times (e.g. a second updater or another node). To keep both from overwriting each other and using up the update limit, the target is paused. Turn off the other updater, then "Update now".
pause_hint.ignored: ipv64 is set to ignore IPv4 or IPv6 from the updater for this domain (e.g. because of DS-Lite/CGNAT). The address was not applied. Set the affected family to "off" here or change the setting at ipv64, then enable the target again.

update.now_hint: Reports the address to ipv64 right away, even without a change. Uses update limit.
update.busy: A sync is running right now. Please try again in a few seconds.
update.nothing: {name}: nothing to report, no current address is known for the selected modes.

limit.own: of which from this node (24 h): {count}
limit.warn: The update limit is almost reached. After that ipv64 accepts no more updates until the reset.

where.online_hint: Measured only by ipv64 at the selected locations
where.hybrid_here: Locally on this node (and possibly others) and online at ipv64
where.hybrid_other: Locally on another node and online at ipv64; this node does not measure it
where.local_here: Measured by this node (possibly also by other nodes)
where.other_hint: Measured only by another node of your account; visible here only

api.title: Online checks at ipv64 (directly via the API)
api.hint: ipv64 measures these checks at its locations; you manage them here directly with your API key. Measuring local checks of this node online as well (hybrid), live states, notifications via ipv64 and syncing your local checks run through the healthchecks sync.
api.empty: No online checks in the account yet.
api.form_hint: This check is saved at ipv64 directly with your API key and measured there at the selected locations. Set notifications in the portal.

proj.check: This check: {n} online checks per day ({sec} s × {locs} location(s)).
proj.local: This check uses no daily quota (local, paused or push).
proj.total: Account total about {n} of {limit} per day (without pushes).
proj.over: That does not last a full day: once the quota is used up, online checks pause until midnight.
proj.runout: At this rate the quota runs out today around {time}; online checks then pause until midnight.

quota.reached: Daily quota for online checks reached ({today} of {limit}). Online checks and push evaluation at ipv64 pause until midnight; local checks of this node keep running.
quota.near: Daily quota for online checks almost reached: {today} of {limit} today. After that, online checks pause until midnight.

hc.sync_rejected_hint: The change only applies locally. Reduce online measuring points (locations, online/hybrid) or upgrade the account class, then save again.

notifier.title: Notifies
notifier.hint: Who sends notifications on a state change. In a local group, the first reachable measuring node.

sources.title: Measuring points
sources.stale_hint: No measurement from this point for a while (node offline or location changed).

diag.inside: Down inside, OK outside: problem in the home network, on the node or the internal path.
diag.outside: OK inside, down outside: internet uplink, port forwarding, DNS or firewall.
diag.both: Down inside and outside: the service itself is affected.

docker.title: Docker containers
docker.subtitle: checked locally via the Docker socket
docker.unwatched: Not monitored yet – click to add:
docker.target_hint: Name or ID of the container on this host (suggestions from the container list).
docker.host_hint: Empty = default. unix:///var/run/docker.sock or tcp://socket-proxy:2375 (e.g. docker-socket-proxy).
docker.rules: Docker checks run only on this node (not online, not movable). Rating: running = OK; healthcheck “unhealthy”, stopped, paused or restart loop = down. When linked to ipv64 the state is reported and visible in the portal too.

hc.run_unreachable: No measuring node reachable (not connected to ipv64?).
hc.run_remote: Measured by ipv64 only; online checks run on their interval.

chart.legend_hint: Click a source in the legend to show only it (again: all), Ctrl-click for several.
chart.note_raw: Single measurements per measuring point; gaps = down.

group.label: Group
group.hint: Checks with the same group are listed together.

hc.empty: No healthchecks yet. Create the first one.
hc.unchecked_detail: No measurement for {ago} – whether the service is reachable right now is unknown. All values on this page are from the last measurement ({time}, state then: {state}).
hc.delete_confirm: Delete check “{name}” with all its data?

owner.online_hint: Checked by ipv64.net only, shown here for reference
owner.other_hint: Belongs to another node of your account, shown here for reference

hc.run_push: Push checks are reported by the service itself.

form.nodes_hint: Several nodes possible, e.g. at different sites or with VPN access. Every selected node measures the check itself and shows up as its own measuring point.
form.nodes_single: Docker checks belong to the node that runs the container and cannot be moved.
form.cert_min_days_hint: HTTPS: report down when the certificate expires in fewer days (0 = off). The expiry date is always read.
form.target_hint_port: Hostname or IP address, without port. Enter the port below.
form.push_hint: After saving, the service calls the push URL regularly. If the call stays away longer than period plus grace, the check counts as down.
form.parent_hint: If the parent is down, this check does not alert on its own.
form.icmp_hint: Ping in a container needs unprivileged ICMP (ping_group_range) or CAP_NET_RAW.
form.stabilize_hint: Successes in a row until OK again
form.invert_hint: Down counts as OK and vice versa.
form.sources_hint: Online and hybrid checks at ipv64 need the healthchecks sync (connection to the hub servers).
form.locations_hint: Multiple locations from account class Supporter. Every online measuring point counts against the class's healthcheck limit, local measurements never do.
form.policy_hint: With several measuring points (node, Nuremberg, Falkenstein) this rule decides when the check counts as down. If only some report a failure, the check is “partially down”.
form.notify_degraded_hint: Only relevant with several measuring points.

push.local_hint: Reachable in your own network. If this node measures the check, the push counts even without internet; ipv64 and other nodes learn about it via the link.
push.online_hint_local: Reachable from anywhere. ipv64 forwards the push to this node while it is connected.
push.online_hint_online: The check is evaluated at ipv64; use this address.
push.title: Push URL
push.hint: Call this URL regularly, e.g. from cron. With ?status=down the service reports an outage itself.

maint.title: Maintenance windows
maint.hint: During a maintenance window checks keep running but do not alert. Measurements are marked and do not count against availability.

hc.empty_hint: Push, HTTP(S), keyword, ping, TCP, port and certificate. Everything stays in your network.

body.quota_local: Local checks of your nodes keep running. More checks per day: longer intervals, fewer locations or a higher account class.

browser.sound_note: Besides the operating system sound, the open page plays a short tone (outage low, recovery high). Browsers allow sound only after the page was clicked once.
browser.title: Browser notifications
browser.intro: Outages and recoveries appear right in the browser – no e-mail or app needed. Create a channel of type “Browser” (it applies to the selected checks like any channel) and switch it on here in every browser.
browser.insecure: Browsers allow system notifications only via HTTPS or localhost.
browser.denied: The browser blocked notifications for this site (lock icon in the address bar).
browser.unsupported: This browser cannot show system notifications.
browser.inpage: Messages then appear at the bottom right of the open page.
browser.note: Only delivered while a Node64 page is open in this browser (a background tab is enough).

twofa.title: Two-factor authentication
twofa.hint: Protects the login with an additional code from an authenticator app.
twofa.enabled: Two-factor authentication enabled. Other sessions were signed out.
twofa.code_wrong: The code does not match. Check the device clock and try again.
twofa.step1: Open your authenticator app (e.g. Aegis, 2FAS, Google Authenticator).
twofa.step2: Scan the QR code or type in the secret.
twofa.recovery_hint: Each code works once if the app is unavailable. Store them safely now, they are not shown again.

apikey.title: API keys
apikey.hint: For scripts and automations against the local API. Usage: Authorization: Bearer <key>.
apikey.name: Name, e.g. backup script
apikey.not_found: This API key does not exist (anymore).
apikey.show_once: The key is shown only now:

reset.title: Reset node
reset.hint: Deletes all local data: checks, measurements, channels, users, settings, keys and backups. The node then starts like a fresh install. A link with ipv64 is removed first.
reset.confirm: Really delete ALL data of this node permanently and restart?
reset.restarting: The node is being reset and restarts. In a few seconds you can set it up again.

backup.title: Backup and configuration
backup.hint: The backup contains the whole database including measurements. The export contains only the configuration as JSON.
backup.restore_hint: The node restarts afterwards. The previous database is kept under /data/backups.
backup.restore_confirm: The current database will be replaced and the node restarted. Continue?
backup.restarting: Database accepted, the node is restarting now. Sign in again in a few seconds.
backup.invalid: This is not a Node64 database.
backup.password_short: The password needs at least 8 characters.
backup.import_hint: Checks are matched by token, channels and maintenance windows by name. Nothing is deleted.
backup.invalid_config: This is not a Node64 configuration file.
backup.password_needed: The file is encrypted, please enter the password.
backup.password_wrong: The password does not match the file.

peer.title: Local group
peer.need_account: A local group needs an ipv64 account on this node: set up the healthchecks sync or enter an API key in the settings. A group only contains nodes of the same account.
peer.hint: Nodes of the same ipv64 account sync healthchecks directly with each other, in the local network over the normal web port, in addition to the healthchecks sync with ipv64.
peer.how_sync: Checks, maintenance windows, measurements and the notification settings are synced between all nodes (within seconds).
peer.how_notify: If several nodes measure a check, exactly one notifies: the first reachable one in the list of measuring nodes. The check shows which one.
peer.fwd_self: This node passes changes of nodes without Healthchecks sync on to ipv64.
peer.fwd_other: “{name}” passes changes of nodes without Healthchecks sync on to ipv64.
peer.fwd_none: No node of the group is linked to ipv64 and reachable: changes and notifications stay within the group.
peer.remove_confirm: Remove “{name}” from the local group? All nodes of the group are told.
peer.add_hint: Shows a code that you enter on the other node under “Join a group”.
peer.code_intro: Enter on the other node under “Join a group”:
peer.addr: Address of a node in the group
peer.self_url_hint: How the other nodes reach this one (suggested: the address you are using right now).
peer.leave_confirm: Leave the local group? The other nodes are told.
peer.err_no_account: This node has no ipv64 account (healthchecks sync or API key missing).
peer.err_account: The other node belongs to a different ipv64 account. A group only contains nodes of the same account.
peer.err_url: The address must start with http:// or https://.

link.key_text: An ipv64 API key for {account} is stored in this container. The node links directly with it, without a code and without signing in on the website. The key is only used to redeem the code; the node gets its own access as always, which you can revoke separately.
link.key_or: Or with a code on the website:
link.key_hint: Tip: with an ipv64 API key in the settings, linking takes one click.
link.key_invalid: ipv64 rejected the API key (invalid or expired). Please check it in the settings.
link.key_failed: Linking with the API key failed: {err}
link.already_linked: This node is already linked to ipv64.
link.key_pending: Code redeemed. The connection follows in a few seconds.
link.key_mismatch: The ipv64 API key in the settings belongs to a different account ({account}, #{key}) than this link (#{link}). DynDNS and healthchecks then run under different accounts.
link.peers_hint: Known via the ipv64 hub servers. Nodes do not connect to each other directly; a check can be measured by several nodes.
link.title: Healthchecks sync with ipv64
link.unavailable: Linking is not available in this installation.
link.local_notifications: Also send my own channels locally while linked
link.local_notifications_hint: Normally ipv64.net sends all notifications so nothing arrives twice. With this option the node additionally sends its own channels itself.
link.unlink_confirm: Unlink? The node keeps running standalone.
link.keep_checks: Keep the {count} checks measured only by this node running at ipv64 as online checks (within the limit). Unchecked, they are deleted at ipv64.
link.scope: Only these {own} checks are affected. The other {other} checks in the account (from other nodes or online checks) stay at ipv64 in any case.
link.code_intro: Enter this code at ipv64.net. It is valid for 10 minutes.
link.step2: Enter the code, choose location and remote management
link.waiting: Waiting for the code to be entered at ipv64.net …
link.intro: Link this node with your ipv64.net account. Everything keeps working locally; the connection goes outbound from the node, no port needs to be opened.
link.benefit1: See and edit checks in the portal from any device
link.benefit2: Have checks verified from Nuremberg and Falkenstein too (hybrid)
link.benefit3: Notifications via ipv64 mail, SMS and app
link.privacy: Note: after linking, configuration and results of this node are sent to ipv64.net – including targets in your home network.
link.start_failed_hint: The node must reach hc-srv01.ipv64.net and hc-srv02.ipv64.net via HTTPS (port 443): check DNS, firewall and clock.
link.conflicts_hint: The same setting was changed here and at ipv64.net while there was no connection. Decide which version applies – nothing is overwritten silently.

dns64.title: DNS64
dns64.not_running: The DNS service is not running.

lists.title: Blocklists
lists.hint: Tick and apply; the DNS service then reloads the lists. “Domains” only counts entries not already in a list above.
lists.add_hint: Formats: hosts file, one domain per line or Adblock syntax (||domain^, exceptions @@||domain^).

allow.title: Allowed domains
allow.not_running: The allowlist can be edited once the DNS service is running.
allow.import_hint: One domain per line, e.g. from the allowlist.txt of the old DNS64 container or a Pi-hole whitelist. Comments (#) and timestamps are ignored, existing entries stay.

up.title: Upstream servers
up.hint: Queries to the internet go encrypted to the configured servers: DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH), DNS-over-TLS (DoT) or DNS-over-QUIC (DoQ). “Fastest in” shows how often a server answered first.

cache.title: DNS cache
cache.hint: Popular domains are renewed shortly before they expire. Expired entries are served instantly for up to 1 hour and refreshed in the background.

settings.title: Settings
settings.port_hint: UDP and TCP. Devices on your network use this host's IP as DNS server, which only works with port 53. Other ports are for testing or when 53 is taken.
settings.router_none: No router found at the moment, local names are not resolved.
settings.router_hint: Names like fritz.box, .lan or single host names only go to this DNS server, never to the internet. IP or IP:port.
settings.anonymize_hint: Shortened or not stored applies to new entries; device names and top clients are then limited or unavailable.
settings.allow_nets_hint: Private networks, Tailscale (100.64.0.0/10) and directly attached private networks and IPv6 /64s are always allowed. Add e.g. another IPv6 prefix or VPN networks here, one per line; 0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0 are not possible.
settings.allow_nets_public: Public networks entered ({nets}): DNS64 answers every device in them, strangers too. Only enter what really belongs to you, and never forward port 53/853 on your router.
settings.refused: {n} queries from foreign addresses refused since start, last {ip} ({time}).
settings.up_hint: Queries to the internet go encrypted to the ticked servers: DoH (HTTPS, port 443), DoT (TLS, port 853) or DoQ (QUIC, port 853). Each server's certificate is verified.
settings.up_mode_hint: Fastest: measures the ticked servers continuously and asks only the fastest (1–3) at once; the others are re-measured briefly every 30 s and step in when one hangs or fails. Parallel: every query to all (fast, but a lot of traffic). In order: always the first, the next only on error.
settings.up_add_hint: https://…/dns-query for DoH, tls://name[:853] for DoT, quic://name[:853] for DoQ. DNS64 needs the bootstrap IPs to reach the server without DNS (required when the address contains a name); the certificate is checked against the name.
settings.notify_upstream: Upstream server failing for more than 3 minutes and back again
settings.notify_lists: Blocklist failed to load three times in a row
settings.notify_hint: Sent to the default channels (not during quiet hours), set up under

setup.title: Setup
setup.router: Enter this host's IP as DNS server in your router (DHCP). Then all devices on your network use DNS64 automatically.
setup.docker: In a container DNS64 needs host networking (network_mode: host), so it sees the real device IPs and finds the router by itself.
setup.later: Encrypted queries from devices (DoH/DoT/DoQ) are on the “Encryption” tab.

records.title: Custom DNS records
records.hint: A = IPv4, AAAA = IPv6, CNAME = other name. *.home.lan covers all names below. For A/AAAA DNS64 also answers reverse lookups (PTR). Custom records win over blocklists and never go to the internet.

err.port: The port must be between 1 and 65535.
err.bind: The address must be an IP (empty = all).
err.router: Enter the router as IP or IP:port.
err.retention: The query log keeps 1 to 90 days.
err.hours: The update interval is 1 to 168 hours.
err.net_any: “{net}” would allow every address (open resolver) and is not possible.
err.no_upstream: At least one upstream server must be on.
err.up_url: “{url}” is not a valid address (https://…, tls://… or quic://…).
err.list_url: “{url}” is not a valid list URL.

err.ttl: The TTL is between 1 and 86,400 seconds.
err.name: Invalid name.
err.cname: A CNAME stands alone: no other record for the same name.

err.cert_id: Please select a certificate from the certificate management.
err.acme_domain: Please choose a valid ipv64 domain.

enc.title: Encrypted on the home network
enc.hint: Devices ask DNS64 encrypted instead of port 53: DNS-over-HTTPS (browsers, Windows, iOS/macOS), DNS-over-TLS (iOS/macOS, Android) and DNS-over-QUIC. The same blocklists, allowlist and allowed networks apply.
enc.ports_hint: DoH uses HTTPS (TCP), DoT TCP and DoQ UDP; defaults are 443 and 853. The DoH port must not be the web interface port.
enc.names_hint: Names devices use to reach DNS64 (e.g. dns.home.lan, as a custom record pointing to the node's IP), one per line. The node's IPs are added to the certificate automatically.
enc.cert_hint: With the own CA, devices install the CA certificate once; it may only vouch for private addresses. Publicly valid without installing anything: Let's Encrypt (card on the right) or an own certificate via NODE64_TLS_CERT/NODE64_TLS_KEY.
enc.howto_apple: iPhone, iPad, Mac: download the profile, install it under Settings → General → VPN & Device Management and, with the own CA, trust it under About → Certificate Trust Settings.
enc.howto_windows: Windows 11: import the CA certificate into “Trusted Root Certification Authorities”, then set DNS manually to the node's IP with DNS-over-HTTPS and the DoH address above.
enc.howto_browser: Firefox/Chrome: secure DNS with the DoH address above; Firefox has its own certificate store (import the CA there).
enc.howto_android: Android “Private DNS” (DoT) only accepts publicly valid certificates, no own CA: set up Let's Encrypt above and enter the name as private DNS provider.
enc.cert_central_hint: Certificates (Let's Encrypt, own CA) are managed in the certificate management; it renews them and DNS64 picks them up without a restart.
enc.central_have: Certificate from the certificate management: {name} ({issuer}), valid until {date}.

acme.title: Let's Encrypt
acme.moved: Let's Encrypt certificates are now created in the certificate management (also via DNS-01 with the ipv64 API key) and selected on the left under “Certificate”. An existing DNS64 certificate was moved there during the update.
acme.mig_failed: The move to the certificate management is still pending ({err}); until then DNS64 keeps serving the previous certificate but does not renew it. Next attempt at the next start.
